hero.headline: Palm Beach County man arrested after 100+ mph chase through Indiantown forces cars off road
hero.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled.

Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly. Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95.

Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody. Tillman was arrested on the following charges: fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph.

Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 with late goals to advance to World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored twice in the final five minutes to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday in the World Cup semifinals in Atlanta.
cards.body:
Argentina scored twice in the final five minutes to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday in the World Cup semifinals in Atlanta. Enzo Fernandez equalized in the 85th minute with a shot from outside the box after receiving a pass from Lionel Messi. Substitute Lautaro Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time from a Messi cross.

England had taken the lead when Anthony Gordon scored in the 55th minute. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks, and Alexis Mac Allister sent a header off the post before Argentina broke through. Martinez said he had told Mac Allister before the match that he would score and win it.

The defending champions will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team was ready to go home sad after England scored but proved themselves after going behind. England captain Harry Kane said the team gave every bit of blood, sweat and tears but falling short was gutting.

The loss marks the third time England has fallen in the World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more rhythm and risk while England played with a feeling of having a lot to lose. Messi, now 39 and likely playing at his last World Cup, is one win away from back-to-back titles. Argentina has eliminated England from the World Cup in 1986, 1998, and now 2026.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County return home after nearly two years of structural damage displacement
cards.body:
Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County are returning home after nearly two years of displacement from their condos. Residents were notified last month they could return to their condos after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe.

Katie Johnson was the first to share with WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. She said she almost didn't believe the news at first, describing it as too good to be true. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return. WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, noting that workers are still moving dirt back under the buildings. She reflected on the effort required to bring residents home, saying it's hard work.

Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. He said some residents had their hearts broken because they wanted to spend the rest of their lives there. Katie Johnson said she feels bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation, thinking of neighbors who cannot return.

Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. He said it's been a terrible two years and the financial toll has been severe. The couple had to drain all their savings accounts and 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. Eric Johnson is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. He described it as a real struggle, saying he would like to say they are finally starting to climb out of it, but it still feels like they're kind of still falling and waiting to start climbing back up.

cards.headline: Florida gas prices jump 20 cents a gallon on Tuesday amid Strait of Hormuz tensions
cards.teaser: Florida gas prices rose about 20 cents a gallon Tuesday as military activity in the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil and wholesale gasoline prices higher.
cards.body:
Florida gas prices rose about 20 cents a gallon Tuesday, catching many drivers off guard as military activity in the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil and wholesale gasoline prices higher. Patrick DeHaan, a petroleum analyst with GasBuddy, said the spike is part of a broader regional trend. He said Florida along with other states are getting engaged in the price cycling jump. Oil prices jumped as did the wholesale price of gasoline, driven by the latest military activity in the Strait of Hormuz.

The sudden hike hit drivers hard. Jalisse Thomas, who was filling up her car in West Palm Beach, said the constant fluctuation is a financial strain. It doesn't go down fast enough, and money doesn't go up either, so it is hard, Thomas said. DeHaan said prices do move in both directions, but the sharp increases simply draw more attention than gradual declines. It's a lot easier to notice a one day 30 cent increase than it is to notice a nickel every day, he said. That nickel every day doesn't add up at the same pace that a 30-cent jump does. DeHaan pointed to a recent example, noting that from May 20 to June 20 of this year, gas prices dropped a dollar a gallon.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County commissioners deny private Christian school proposal in Jupiter Farms
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County commissioners voted to deny a controversial proposal to build a large private Christian school in Jupiter Farms after hours of emotional public debate over traffic, growth and the future of the community's rural character.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County commissioners voted to deny a controversial proposal to build a large private Christian school in Jupiter Farms after hours of emotional public debate over traffic, growth and the future of the community's rural character. The proposal from Calvary Church would have brought a K-12 private Christian school to a vacant site on Indiantown Road with plans for nearly 1,000 students. Palm Beach County Mayor Sara Baxter was the only commissioner to vote in favor of the project, citing the need for private Christian education in the area. The county's Zoning Commission Board had already voted unanimously last month to recommend denial of the proposal.

For more than three hours, residents lined up to speak with traffic emerging as one of the contentious topics of the night. One speaker told commissioners that preserving the rural residential and equestrian character of Jupiter is the objective of county plans, noting the scale of the proposed school is larger than the proposed Home Depot and has more customers in it. Supporters pushed back, arguing the school could actually reduce traffic in some cases. One resident said they have a vision of grandkids riding their bike to school that doesn't create any traffic and noted there will be fewer buses. Commissioners questioned details presented by county staff and project representatives, including concerns from the zoning board that development would cover roughly 80 percent of the property. Project officials disputed that interpretation, explaining that required buffer landscaping between the school and nearby homes was being counted as development along with a planned lake on the site.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with 2-0 win over France
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010.
cards.body:
Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot in the 22nd minute after teenager Lamine Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne in the penalty area. A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal raced in from behind to challenge Digne, who was trying to clear the ball after a poor first touch with his head. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, who was playing in his 63rd game for France six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament. Pedro Porro's goal in the 58th minute came on a give-and-go with Dani Olmo to put Spain up 2-0.

Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. They face each other on Wednesday in Atlanta. Kylian Mbappé and France, FIFA's top-ranked team, were trying to become only the third team to reach three consecutive World Cup finals. France will instead play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium. This win marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match.

hero.headline: Martin County residents can get free pool alarms from Safe Kids Treasure Coast
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents.
hero.body:
Safe Kids Treasure Coast and the Florida Department of Health are providing free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents while supplies last. The organizations are asking residents to fill out a survey to determine their eligibility for the drowning prevention program.

The pool alarms are being offered as part of a safety initiative to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools. According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection but should always be used in combination with close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education. The alarms are not intended to replace other safety measures but rather to supplement existing drowning prevention efforts.

Residents interested in obtaining a free pool alarm must complete an eligibility survey. The coalition noted that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free device. Recipients will need to purchase and install the battery separately before the alarm can function properly.

The program is available to Martin County residents with residential pools, with a limited supply of alarms available on a first-come, first-served basis. For more information about the free pool alarm program or questions regarding eligibility requirements, residents can contact Safe Kids Treasure Coast at (772) 462-3501.

cards.headline: England and Argentina renewed fierce World Cup rivalry in semifinal
cards.teaser: England and Argentina met in the World Cup semifinals in Atlanta on Wednesday, continuing one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer.
cards.body:
The World Cup rivalry between the nations dates back to 1962, but it was England's 1-0 win in the quarterfinals four years later that saw it intensify. Argentina captain Antonio Rattin, whose death was announced on Saturday, was sent off in a bad-tempered match. England went on to win the World Cup for the first, and still the only time, in its history. Twenty years on in Mexico, Diego Maradona scored the infamous Hand of God goal that helped Argentina to a 2-1 win in the quarterfinals on the way to becoming world champion for a second time. That game also saw Maradona score what many believe to be the greatest World Cup goal ever when he dribbled the ball from the halfway line before beating England goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

England felt aggrieved again in 1998 when David Beckham was sent off for kicking out at Argentina midfielder Diego Simeone before losing the round-of-16 game on penalties. Beckham got his revenge four years later by scoring a penalty in a 1-0 win that contributed to Argentina being eliminated at the group stage. The two teams meet in Atlanta on Wednesday and the winner will play Spain in the final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday. Neither team has had a smooth ride to the semifinals. Argentina survived scares against Cape Verde and Egypt earlier in the knockout rounds and needed extra time to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in the quarterfinals.

cards.headline: Police investigate death of South Africa World Cup player Jayden Adams
cards.teaser: Police are investigating the death of South Africa World Cup soccer player Jayden Adams after his body was discovered at a property in Cape Town.
cards.body:
Police said Monday they are investigating the death of South Africa World Cup soccer player Jayden Adams, after his body was discovered this weekend at a property in the city of Cape Town. Cape Town central police registered an inquest for investigation following the discovery of the body of a 25-year-old male on Saturday. Police said the body was discovered at a property in the Cape Town neighborhood of Schotsche Kloof at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. Authorities have not released a cause of death. The 25-year-old Adams died two weeks after helping South Africa reach the knockout stage of a World Cup for the first time.

Adams' father, Juanito Adams, told South African TV news station eNCA on Sunday that the family were waiting for the results of an autopsy and had not yet made any funeral plans. Adams played in all three of South Africa's group games as it produced its best performance at the World Cup. He did not feature in the 1-0 loss to Canada in the round of 32 on June 28. South Africa Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said Adams had played in his team's group game against Czech Republic hours after learning that his grandmother had died. There were moments of silence and tributes for Adams at the England vs. Switzerland World Cup quarterfinal games on Saturday.

cards.headline: World Cup semifinals set with four highest-ranked teams
cards.teaser: England and Argentina advanced to join France and Spain in the World Cup semifinals after quarterfinal victories over the weekend.
cards.body:
England advanced to the World Cup semifinals after defeating Norway, with Jude Bellingham scoring twice to lead his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. Argentina also reached the final four by beating Switzerland, with Julián Alvarez scoring in extra time with assistance from a controversial VAR call. Despite the tournament featuring underdog success stories and surprise results, the four highest-ranked teams made it to the semifinals.

Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition for England, and the team would have been knocked out earlier without these two players. Argentina has scored the most goals of any team in the competition with 17 and benefits from experience, as many current squad members won the title in 2022. France is considered by many to be the tournament favorite, with Kylian Mbappé proving highly effective with his pace and directness. He is supported by Ousmane Dembélé and other attackers. Spain beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024, a tournament it won, and also defeated France in the Nations League last year. Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament. The World Cup final is scheduled for July 19.

cards.headline: Atlanta police increased security for England-Argentina World Cup semifinal
cards.teaser: Police and security presence was boosted for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal in Atlanta due to longstanding tensions between the two nations.
cards.body:
Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta. Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War. Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend.

Argentina is the defending champion and has claimed three World Cup titles in addition to being the tournament's runner-up twice. England has not won a World Cup since 1966. It is also the first time since England's World Cup win in 1966 that its national team has earned a berth in the semifinals.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: Vero Beach parents sue city over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed and reburied without consent
hero.teaser: Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo allege their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and reinterred without their knowledge.
hero.body:
Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo have filed an amended lawsuit against the City of Vero Beach alleging their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance work at Crestlawn Cemetery and reburied without their knowledge or consent. The couple's son, identified in court documents only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old and was buried at the city-owned cemetery. According to the complaint, sometime between the 2007 burial and April 2025, heavy equipment being used for maintenance or irrigation work near the burial site breached the grave, damaging or destroying the casket, its contents, and the child's remains.

The lawsuit alleges that someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket, and reinter the child without notifying the parents or obtaining their consent. The parents say they did not learn about what allegedly happened until April 2025, nearly 18 years after their son's burial. The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment.

This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false but rather a ruling that the legal claims as originally pleaded could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The parents have now refiled with different legal arguments in an attempt to overcome the previous dismissal. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint.

The City of Vero Beach has declined to comment on the amended complaint. However, in court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage described by the parents. The city submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C. The case highlights the legal protections cities have under Florida law and the challenges families face when seeking accountability for alleged mishandling of cemetery operations. The amended complaint represents the parents' continued effort to hold the city responsible for what they describe as the unauthorized disturbance and reburial of their infant son's remains.
